messages:
incident-bot: [P1] DEDICATED POOL GPU EXHAUSTION for tenant AcmeCorp in us-west-2. 92% of requests are queuing. Auto-scaler attempted 2x but hit per-tenant cap. Paging maya (oncall) and platform.

maya (oncall): saw the page. jumping on it. currently 502 spikes and request latency > 10s for long-running chat calls. grabbing logs.

juan (sre): logs show OOM throttles and scheduler throttling on pool `dedicated-acme-usw2`. kube events: PodPending scheduling failure: "Insufficient nvidia/gpu"

maya (oncall): can we burst to shared burst-pool? what's the tenant isolation policy here? we need a quick mitigation for customer-facing SLA.

alex (platform): burst to shared pool requires tenant opt-in flag and account-level burst credits. AcmeCorp is on dedicated-only contract (no auto-burst). we can do an emergency manual override but need approval from product/finance for billing. technically doable: copy routing rule to route 10% of traffic to `shared-burst-usw2` with model downgrade.

tara (eng-runtime): quick wins: 1) enable model fallback to smaller variant (redwood/llama-3b-quant) for non-critical calls 2) enable prefix KV caching for repeated sessions 3) throttle token limits per request. I can flip fallback via runtime config in ~4-6m.

nina (account-exec): pinging AcmeCorp contacts. we need to get their ops to allow temporary burst or accept degraded throughput. will call now.

acme-oncall-bot: Monitoring alert forwarded to customer on-call: AcmeCorp-Oncall. Contact: ops-acme@acme.com, phone +1-555-0199.

maya (oncall): proposed immediate mitigations: a) emergency manual burst to shared pool for 30m for high-priority routes only (chat.openai-like) b) runtime fallback to 3B model for non-critical routes c) apply token caps at 4096 and throttle excessive concurrent sessions from the same API key. Who can implement a) now?

alex (platform): I can do the routing change. command I'll run:
```
# copy route and apply override
redwoodctl route copy --src tenant:acme --dst pool:shared-burst-usw2 --filter "route in (chat-priority)" --weight 10
redwoodctl quota set --tenant acme --burst-emergency true
```
Need confirmation from security and legal for temporary exception; but for 30m we can tag emergency.

juan (sre): I'll start evicting low-priority background jobs in the dedicated pool to free GPUs. Running drain on non-critical nodes now: `kubectl cordon node/gpu-n2` -> `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. ETA ~3m to get 1-2 GPUs back.

tara (eng-runtime): I've prepared the fallback config. flipping now for routes `chat-standard` and `chat-bulk`: enabling `model.fallback=redwood/llama-3b-quant`, `cache.kv=true`.

maya (oncall): rolling both measures. alex, proceed with routing override. juan, keep evicting. nina, keep customer updated and get sign-off for emergency billing.

nina (account-exec): on call with AcmeCorp. they approve temporary burst for 30 minutes and accept 10% reroute + model fallback. requesting written confirmation after.

incident-bot: change recorded: route override applied by alex at 1845128078. new route weight: 10% to shared-burst-usw2 for high-priority chat.

maya (oncall): seeing latency drop to ~350-450ms for priority routes, overall queuing reduced. still some 5s tails for bulk tasks.

juan (sre): freed 2 GPUs from background eviction, returning to pool available. still 85% usage. monitoring.

tara (eng-runtime): fallback is active; we see token cost drop ~2.3x for routed requests. QA: check quality regressions; logging flagged ~0.5% increase in NER mismatch for edge evals.

maya (oncall): customer impact update: priority chat restored near-SLA; bulk workloads may be degraded. Acme customer ops confirmed degraded bulk is acceptable for 30m.

alex (platform): scheduling a postmortem action: review per-tenant capacity caps, implement emergency-burst workflow that doesn't require finance approval for short windows. created task in backlog: RED-798.

juan (sre): recommendation: add proactive watermark alerts at 75% and automatic cold-start prewarm to keep headroom. I'll draft runbook updates.

maya (oncall): handing off to juan for monitoring and follow-up. leaving oncall at 1845128240. if anything regresses ping #eng-oncall.

juan (sre): taking over. current status: stabilised. will wait 20m, then rollback overrides and reconcile billing tags.

incident-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged resolved at 1845128250. Summary: dedicated pool exhaustion for AcmeCorp due to sudden spike in long-running chats. Mitigations: manual route burst (10%) to shared pool, model fallback to 3B for non-critical routes, eviction of low-priority jobs. Customer notified and approved. Postmortem: RED-798 assigned to platform + SRE.
